What's new in Vekrun 0.5.1 — Runs that sort themselves out

• An agent fixes its own VM: a missing system package or database extension (pgvector and the like) is the agent's to install, never yours, and a fix that works is remembered, so the VM that proves the work, and every later run of the project, have it from the start.
• No more paying for the same failure: when a test fails the same way twice, the Coordinator steps in; a third time, the run stops with one clear message instead of trying again.
• A Work Item has a $5 spending cap by default. At the cap it pauses and tells you where to raise it; press Run again to go on.
• A message you send just as a run ends is no longer lost: a stopped Work Item runs again with it, work waiting for your review is revised, and only delivered work gets a follow-up.
• Updating while work is running: "Install when safe" now really installs, by itself, as soon as the work is done. Install now asks first, says what stops, and installs straight away.
• Updating a coding agent (Codex and the others) takes one click: the button shows "Starting…" at once while Vekrun checks this Mac.
• Vekrun fits every screen: the sidebar folds to icons in a narrow window, card grids and tab rows reflow, and settings stack instead of scrolling sideways. Setting descriptions are in plain words.
• Tool versions show what's really installed: a tool you updated (in Vekrun or outside it) no longer shows its old version as behind, a version that couldn't be checked says so instead of "Up to date", and on macOS 13 Ollama says it's the newest that runs there.
• After installing or updating a coding agent, Sign in and Done show properly instead of appearing only on hover.
• Work Anywhere installs DigitalOcean's and Hetzner's CLIs for you with one click, then opens their sign-in; the sheet carries on by itself once you're signed in.
• Claude Code: "How models are chosen" checks the sign-in the Factory really uses, so it no longer says "not signed in" after you've connected. While you sign in, a box for the page's code is always there, and if Claude Code finishes on its own, Vekrun says the code isn't needed.
• The agents' measurements read plainly: "Can run offline" instead of "Local" (Codex isn't using that model, it could), Claude Code's cost no longer says it reports only tokens, and agents with no runs say so once.
• Production monitoring shows which system each error comes from: the Honeybadger, Datadog, Sentry, AppSignal or GitHub logo on every card and on its details.
• The code editor no longer freezes on big projects: opening a folder asks Git about all its files at once instead of one at a time (a 181-file folder went from 3.8 s to about 50 ms), and the editor's file, search, index and Git status work runs off the window's thread.
• "Triage now" is now "Investigate new errors", and it really investigates: each new error at or above the severity you set (error by default) gets the same read-only investigation as Investigate, one at a time, up to 3 a day. Every card shows where its investigation is, investigations keep going when you leave the page, and each report appears in the error's details. Before, it only marked errors as investigating.
• Production monitoring's Connections open in a proper dialog: one card per provider with its logo, how it's signed in, when it last synced and which applications it watches, with Choose applications and Sync now up front and the rest under More. Browser sign-ins no longer say "token missing", and the investigations strip names the error instead of a number.
• Coding agents can take Factory roles: picking Claude Code or Codex for a role no longer shows "adapters are off" refusals (Factory runs already used them), and the check reads the sign-in Factory runs use.
